material_limitations: These are separate legislative events.
The measures may differ beyond their shared stated purpose.

competing_interpretations: Treat wording and timing differences as too material for one repeated-pattern proposition.

episode_semantic_evidence.single-119-hconres-38-2-85: Whether to adopt H.Con.Res. 38, which would direct the President pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution to remove United States Armed Forces from unauthorized hostilities in the Islamic Republic of Iran.

episode_semantic_evidence.single-119-hconres-75-2-170: Whether to adopt H.Con.Res. 75, which would direct the President, pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove the United States Armed Forces from hostilities against the Islamic Republic of Iran.
episode_semantic_evidence.single-119-hconres-86-2-199: Whether to adopt H.Con.Res. 86, which would direct the President, pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities with Iran.
episode_semantic_evidence.single-119-hconres-89-2-282: Whether to adopt H.Con.Res. 89, which would direct the President, pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities with Iran.

material_limitations: The resolutions are separate events with small wording differences, including with, against, and unauthorized hostilities.
The pattern does not establish that the factual hostilities or legal posture were unchanged across dates.
accepted_candidate_content.proposition: Across five separate resolutions, Foushee supported directing removal of United States Armed Forces from hostilities with or against Iran under the War Powers Resolution.
accepted_candidate_content.rationale: Each accepted episode meaning independently states the same removal mechanism and Iran-hostilities target, and all five accepted episode directions support it.

relevant_contrasts.reason: A different War Powers target and repeal of earlier AUMFs use different targets or mechanisms and do not enlarge the Iran pattern.

competing_interpretations: Retain the two choices only as separate episodes because each resolution may reflect a distinct factual context.

competing_interpretations: Treat the wording and session difference as too material for a repeated-pattern proposition.

relevant_contrasts.reason: Other War Powers resolutions concern different targets; shared mechanism alone does not merge country-specific propositions.

episode_semantic_evidence.single-119-hr-3106-2-234: Whether to pass H.R. 3106, which would require the Secretary of Homeland Security to conduct a collective response to a terrorism exercise that includes the management of cascading effects on critical infrastructure during times of extreme cold weather, and for other purposes.

An accepted Justice calibration relationship exists for this pair but contributes no National Security authority; this candidate derives independently from the accepted M11F episodes.

accepted_candidate_content.rationale: The accepted National Security episode meanings independently establish two federal terrorism-preparedness requirements, and both accepted directions support them.

competing_interpretations: Retain the whole-measure authorization separately because it is structurally different from the three amendments.

episode_semantic_evidence.single-119-hamdt-57-1-209: Whether to adopt H.Amdt. 57. The official exact-amendment description states: “An amendment numbered 116 printed in Part A of House Report 119-199 to strike funds from being used for assistance to Ukraine.”
episode_semantic_evidence.single-119-hamdt-93-1-255: Whether to adopt H.Amdt. 93. The official exact-amendment description states: “An amendment numbered 22 printed in Part A of House Report 119-255 to prohibit assistance to Ukraine.”
episode_semantic_evidence.single-119-hr-2913-2-207: Whether to pass H.R. 2913, which would authorize support for Ukraine, and for other purposes.

material_limitations: The three restrictive amendments differ in scope.
H.R. 2913 is a whole measure and includes ‘other purposes’.
No position is inferred on any H.R. 2913 component beyond its accepted bounded whole-measure meaning.
accepted_candidate_content.proposition: Across four separate Ukraine-assistance choices, Foushee opposed three amendments that would restrict or prohibit assistance and supported a measure authorizing support for Ukraine.
accepted_candidate_content.rationale: The accepted episode meanings establish three distinct assistance restrictions and one whole-measure authorization; their accepted directions mechanically produce a mixed Semantic IR direction.

competing_interpretations: Keep the armed-forces support prohibition distinct from the broader account reductions.

episode_semantic_evidence.single-119-hamdt-56-1-208: Whether to adopt H.Amdt. 56. The official exact-amendment description states: “Amendment sought to strike funding to support the armed forces of Jordan.”

H.Amdt. 236 has a broader funding/account scope.
The mechanisms and affected accounts are not claimed to be identical.
accepted_candidate_content.proposition: Across two separate amendments, Foushee opposed reductions or prohibitions on United States assistance to Jordan.
accepted_candidate_content.rationale: Both accepted meanings describe amendments reducing or prohibiting Jordan assistance, and both accepted episode directions oppose those amendments.

competing_interpretations: Keep the health-care, information-form, facilities, service-eligibility, and school-athletics mechanisms separate.

episode_semantic_evidence.single-119-hamdt-256-2-268: Whether to adopt H.Amdt. 256. The official exact-amendment description states: “Amendment prohibits male participation in female sports at Department of Defense Education Activity schools.”
episode_semantic_evidence.single-119-hamdt-86-1-246: Whether to adopt H.Amdt. 86. The official exact-amendment description states: “Amendment prohibits the Department of Defense from covering or furnishing gender-related medical treatment under TRICARE.”
episode_semantic_evidence.single-119-hamdt-88-1-248: Whether to adopt H.Amdt. 88. The official exact-amendment description states: “Amendment prohibits the Secretary of Defense from soliciting information through a form or survey regarding the gender identity of an individual, providing an option to indicate the sex or gender of an individual is something other than male or female, and requires the Secretary reject a response other than male or female to a required question on a form or survey regarding sex or gender.”
episode_semantic_evidence.single-119-hamdt-89-1-249: Whether to adopt H.Amdt. 89. The official exact-amendment description states: “Amendment prohibits individuals from accessing or using single-sex spaces on military installations which do not correspond to the biological sex of the individual.”

material_limitations: These are different mechanisms.
They affect different populations and settings.
The proposition is confined to the five enumerated military/DoD choices.
It does not establish a broader position outside these contexts.
accepted_candidate_content.proposition: Across five separate amendments, Foushee opposed military or Department of Defense restrictions involving gender-related health care or biological-sex-based requirements for service, forms, facilities, or school athletics.
accepted_candidate_content.rationale: The five accepted episode meanings enumerate bounded military or DoD restrictions and all five accepted episode directions oppose them.
